experiment.title: Making the hit feel different from the cast
experiment.hypothesis: Can damage-only ground rings or fighter reactions preserve the stronger impact you liked while separating casting from taking damage?

variants.name: Previous cues
variants.description: The previous B, preserved as a reference: preparation rings, release rings and hit crosses.

variants.name: Damage rings · release sparks
variants.description: Warm airborne sparks mark release; only damage makes a ground ring. Softer preparation and stronger melee/ice contrast.

variants.name: Fighter flash · impact sparks
variants.description: The hurt fighter briefly flashes and compresses, with impact sparks instead of damage rings. Shares the revised preparation, release and spell contrast.

simulationVariants.name: Bursts and resets
simulationVariants.description: Slower neutral travel, faster sprints and dashes, planted recovery. Does contrast create momentum or more circling?

evidenceLimits: Each setup runs once with C/burst gameplay. All visual alternatives use that same trace; these are not independent combat treatments.
Gameplay logs locate evidence; they cannot establish visual readability or experienced pacing.
Screening evidence; no owner preference or balance validation yet.
Damage gaps are descriptive, not a score for entertainment or tension.
Rotations test layout sensitivity, not swapping asymmetric fighter kits.
Current telemetry has spell-type IDs, not unique cast/projectile causal IDs. Do not attribute a dodge to a specific incoming attack.
Raw rejected-cast diagnostics are retained in JSONL and omitted from the curated event excerpts.
